newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Solid start for Solidbank.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Solid start for Solidbank.

text.p: Asian debt markets were slowly getting back into the swing of things after year-end holidays with a new issue for the Philippines' Solidbank.
The three-year floating rate certificate of deposit was launched at par to float at 85 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate. There are no puts or calls.
With fees, the certificates pay an all-in return of 92.5 basis points to co-lead managers and 91.5 basis points to senior managers.
Bank of Nova Scotia, Dresdner Southeast Asia and Sakura Finance Asia are arrangers and lead managers.
Solidbank's prior issue, a three-year FRCD launched in early February 1996, paid much more, offering an all-in return of 125 basis points to the top tier.
Since then, however, pricing for Philippine bank credits have come in sharply on views that the economy is improving.

Investor confidence in the Philippines received a big boost last September when the government successfully swapped Brady bonds for uncollateralized paper in the form of a 20-year fixed rate sovereign bond issue.
While bankers expect Philippine issues to continue attracting interest this year, many said price spreads are unlikely to show the same sharp contraction as in 1996.
"I think that this year is going to be a year of consolidation in terms of pricing for Philippines issues. I wouldn't expect to see that much more tightening," one banker said.
The Philippines has mandated JP Morgan and CS First Boston to lead a 30-year Yankee bond in the first half of this year. JP Morgan arranged the Brady swap.
Philippine finance secretary Roberto de Ocampo also has said that the Philippines plans to issue Europeso bonds on a limited basis in first-half 1997.
A number of issues for Philippine banks and companies also are in the pipeline, bankers said.
Elsewhere, bankers are waiting to see which South Korean bank will bring the first deal of the year and at what pricing.
